title: E0107: Weak Random for Security Tokens
plain_english: Generating security-sensitive tokens (session tokens, CSRF tokens, password reset tokens, API keys) with weak random number generators like `rand()`, `mt_rand()`, or `uniqid()` can make them predictable.
why_matters: Weak random values are predictable. Attackers can: - Guess session tokens and hijack user sessions - Predict CSRF tokens and bypass CSRF protection - Guess password reset tokens and take over accounts - Recover API keys and access protected resources
good_example:
$token = bin2hex(random_bytes(16));   // cryptographically secure
$resetToken = random_int(100000, 999999); // cryptographically secure
what_it_checks: `rand()`, `mt_rand()`, or `uniqid()` used for security-sensitive purposes (tokens, keys, salts)
`mt_rand()` or `rand()` assigned to variables named `token`, `key`, `secret`, `salt`, `nonce`, or `csrf`
